instantiated_cells.justification: Section 13.62(11) defines lobbyist broadly as an individual employed by or contracting with a principal, covering both contract and in-house lobbyists; §13.695 separately requires agencies to file statements identifying employees who lobby.
The definitions section §13.62 does not define "public entity"; it defines "agency" instead, and no term "public entity" appears in the statute.

The law contains materiality thresholds: an individual is only a lobbyist if making lobbying communications on at least 5 days per reporting period (§13.62(11)), and principals spending under $500/year are exempt from registration (§13.621(5), §13.64(1)).

Lobbying is defined as influencing legislative or administrative action by communication with elective state officials, agency officials, or legislative employees; "legislative action" includes the governor's approval/veto and "elective state official" includes the governor.

Targets include elective state officials, agency officials (members, officers, employees, consultants of agencies), and legislative employees (members/officers of legislature and staff), covering both legislative and executive/administrative branches.
The definition covers communications with elective state officials (including the governor) and agency officials to influence legislative or administrative action.
The lobbying definition encompasses communications with elective state officials (governor included per §13.62(6) and §5.02(23)) and agency officials.
Lobbying definition explicitly includes communications with elective state officials, agency officials, and legislative employees to influence legislative or administrative action.

Targets of lobbying include the legislative branch (legislative employees, members/officers of the legislature) and the executive/administrative branch (agency officials including members, officers, employees, consultants).

Section 13.621(3) exempts elective state officials, local officials, tribal officials, and legislative employees acting in their official capacity from registration/reporting requirements, so they are not required to register.

The lobbyist definition uses compensation (economic consideration beyond expense reimbursement) and time (5-day threshold per reporting period) standards; local and tribal officials are excluded if not principally employed to influence legislative/administrative action, and state agency employees are covered under §13.695.

The definitions in §13.62 do not rely on public charter or special government protection; the lobbyist/principal definitions turn on employment, compensation, and lobbying activity, not on charter status.
No definition in §13.62 turns on ownership; "business entity" is defined broadly (§13.62(5)) but ownership is not a triggering criterion for lobbyist/principal status.
No statutory definition in §13.62 relies on revenue structure or composition; thresholds are based on lobbying expenditures ($500) and days of communication (5 days), not revenue composition.
